questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country, a country that I really wanted to visit, student accomandation through the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: University of Sydney is an amazing place to be exchange student!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It always take time to find out how to navigate in a new country, but Jane, the person in charge of exchange students from USYD did a very good job!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I attended different welcome events.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Queen Mary Bulding. It is not completely on campus, but quite close to, and everyone that lives there study on USYD.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: One big kitchen for 800 people on the ground floor. It is a very interesting experience, but it works actually better than you think.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It works super good and is a very social doorm. Especially in the begining, when you don't know that many people, it is great to live in a big dorm where all exchange students live. Remeber to apply as soon as you get the mail from Jane! The rooms get taking within one or two days.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Ypu apply from home, but you can't see your schedule before you actually arrive in Sydney, so you probally have to redo your schedule and courses when ypu arrive because your classes clash. It is quite difficult and takes a lot of time because you have to make your schedule yourself (which is different from KU), but it works out in the end and Jane helps a lot!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can book meetings with Jane to get help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting all the classes I wanted to, but it was a big work, because some of the classes I had first had lectures at the same times, so I had to choose some new ones.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take some of the fun exchange student classes! I had "Learning in Outdoor Education", which was super fun and a good way to meet all the exchange students from all over the world. The teachers Wayne and Sam are amazing!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The classes are easier than in denmark, even though I took graduate BA courses. We were not allowed to take master classes when we were on BA.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar with lectures, tutorials and lab. A big difference is that most of the classes are mandatory! And you collect parts of your grade through out the semester, by handing in assignments etc, so your final exam doesn't count the whole grade. This was actually really nice when you are on exchange!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CHEM3122 Molecular Self Assembly
 CHEM3123 Computational Chemistry
 EDUH4052 Learning in Outdoor Education
 INFO1110 Introduction to Programming

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Learning in Outdoor Education and Sport and Leaning in Australian culture are both exchange courses for fun, which is super nice! Both my chemistry courses were also good - I prefered Computational Chemistry since there was a lot of lab work in Molecular Self Assembly which was a bit boring in the end, because USYD is very stricht about lab, so we didn't get to do that cool things... Programming was a nice way to learn python, and the course is structered so you get your grade after how far you get in the course, like how many assignments and tests you pass. It is easy to see ehat your end grade is and you can stop when you are satisfied.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spend most of my money on travelling during and after the semester.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent is super expensive in Sydney:( 7.500 kr as in Queen Mary Building is some of the cheapest you can live.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The student union at USYD is amazing and has so many acitivites to offer!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything you can imagine!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: USU which is the student union has everything! FoodHub is a place where you can get free food and groceries every day - it is a good way to save some money!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Blue Mountains (2 hours away from Sydney), Hunter Valley (3 hours away from Sydney), the different beaches, CBD. There are lots of things to see and do!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Sydney is very westers and feels quite a lot like copenhagens, except it's way bigger.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I met most local students in my chemistry classes. Outside of classes you mostly meet exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The professors speak quite fast english with strong australian accent, it can be a bit difficult in the beginning but you get used to it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Aussies are very open and talk a lot! When you go grocery shopping, wait in a line or something, you always start talking to people! It is so nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Attent all the welcome events and social events to meet people in the begining!
Don't take too difficult classes, you will spend a lot of time traveling and having fun with your new friends, so you don't have time to study a lot ;)
Apply to Queen Mary Building for accomendation, it is very easy to live there. It is nothing special and far away from the beach, but it is the easiest way to meet new people!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Save up a lot of money before you go! And apply for as many scholarships as possible - but it is difficult to get them as a BA student.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people I have met from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Speaking english the whole time, but I improved my english a lot!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
